tagline: Joint BMDO + NASA lunar orbiter — first global multispectral map and first bistatic-radar evidence for polar water ice
description: Officially the Deep Space Program Science Experiment (DSPSE). Conceived by the Ballistic Missile Defense Organization to qualify lightweight sensors in deep-space conditions, with NASA collaborating on lunar + asteroid science. Launched 1994-01-25 on a Titan IIG, entered lunar polar orbit 1994-02-19 for 71 days of mapping. Imaged every square kilometre of the Moon at 100-300 m resolution across 11 wavelengths — the first complete global lunar map. The bistatic radar experiment using Clementine's transmitter and DSN ground antennas found enhanced echoes at south-polar Shackleton crater consistent with water ice, predating LCROSS by 15 years. A failed thruster firing aborted the planned Geographos asteroid flyby and ended the mission.
best_known_for: First complete global lunar multispectral map and first hint of polar water ice — 1994
